Section 4.2(b)(i) of Executive Order 14110 provides that, until the Secretary of Commerce defines the technical conditions, the Secretary shall require compliance with the reporting requirements for any model trained using more than 10^26 integer or floating-point operations, or more than 10^23 operations if trained primarily on biological sequence data.

The Seoul Ministerial Statement recognises that severe risks could be posed by a model or system capability to meaningfully assist non-state actors in the development, production, acquisition or use of chemical or biological weapons.

Version 1.0 of the AI Safety Governance Framework lists, as a technical countermeasure, strict screening of training data to ensure it contains no sensitive data from high-risk fields such as nuclear, biological, chemical and missile weapons.

Version 1.0 of the AI Safety Governance Framework lists improving the traceability of AI systems' end use, to prevent their use in high-risk scenarios such as manufacturing nuclear, biological, chemical or missile weapons of mass destruction.

RSP v2.0 states that its CBRN weapons Capability Threshold is the ability to significantly help individuals or groups with basic technical backgrounds (e.g., undergraduate STEM degrees) create/obtain and deploy CBRN weapons.

Measure 6.1 of the initial draft commits signatories to treat six types as systemic risks: cyber offence; chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear risks; loss of control; automated use of models for AI research and development; persuasion and manipulation; and large-scale discrimination.

NIST states that the second public draft of NIST AI 800-1 revises the initial public draft, adding appendices on measuring misuse risk and on chemical/biological and cybersecurity misuse risk and content on open models and the AI supply chain.

Frontier Governance Framework (February 2025) states that the High risk level for CBRN weapons is described by two capability statements: a meaningful uplift to an expert’s (PhD level education in related fields) ability to develop and deliver a novel CBRN threat, and a meaningful uplift to a medium-skilled actor’s (e.g., STEM education) ability to develop and deliver a known CBRN threat.

Frontier AI Framework v1.1 states that a model is at the high risk threshold when it provides significant uplift towards execution of a threat scenario but does not enable execution of any threat scenario identified as potentially sufficient to produce a catastrophic outcome.

Frontier AI Framework v1.1 states that if evaluation results indicate a frontier AI has a “high” risk threshold by providing significant uplift towards realization of a catastrophic outcome, Meta will not release it externally.

Appendix 1.4 of the chapter treats four risks as specified systemic risks for systemic risk identification: chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear risks; loss of control; cyber offence; and harmful manipulation.

SB 53 defines 'catastrophic risk' as a foreseeable and material risk that a frontier developer's development, storage, use or deployment of a frontier model will materially contribute to the death of, or serious injury to, more than 50 people, or to more than $1 billion in damage to, or loss of, property, arising from a single incident in which a frontier model (a) provides expert-level assistance in creating or releasing a chemical, biological, radiological or nuclear weapon; (b) engages without meaningful human oversight in a cyberattack or in conduct that would be murder, assault, extortion or theft if committed by a human; or (c) evades the control of its developer or user. Stated exclusions apply.

FAIF (December 2025) states that xAI developed an internal benchmark of benign and restricted biology and chemistry related queries in collaboration with SecureBio and that its risk acceptance criteria for system deployment is maintaining an answer rate of less than 1 out of 20 on restricted queries.

Frontier Governance Framework (February 2026) states that the High risk level for CBRN weapons is described by two capability statements: a meaningful uplift to an expert’s (PhD level education in related fields) ability to develop and deliver a novel CBRN threat, and a meaningful uplift to a medium-skilled actor’s (e.g., STEM education) ability to develop and deliver a known CBRN threat.

RSP v3.0 states that its non-novel chemical/biological weapons production threshold covers AI systems with the ability to significantly help individuals or groups with basic technical backgrounds (e.g., undergraduate STEM degrees) create/obtain and deploy chemical and/or biological weapons with serious potential for catastrophic damages.
